items.title: More than 200,000 students get another long weekend in Mississauga, Brampton, Caledon
items.summary: More than 200,000 students in Mississauga, Brampton, Caledon and parts of Dufferin County will get another three-day weekend, with a scheduled day off school on Monday, Oct. 26. The day off is a professional activity (PA) day, giving teachers time for professional development while students stay home. The Peel District School Board and Dufferin-Peel Catholic District School Board have coordinated their calendars so that elementary and secondary students will be off on the same day. The PA day also falls on Ontario’s municipal election day, meaning students will return to class on Tuesday, Oct. 27. It’s the second consecutive weekend that students have enjoyed three days off, following the Thanksgiving long weekend earlier this month. The Oct. 26 break is part of the regular school calendar, with several more holidays, PA days and school breaks scheduled between now and the end of the 2026-27 school year. Families can expect several more opportunities for students to take a break from the classroom over the coming months. The following dates apply to Peel District School Board and Dufferin-Peel Catholic District School Board schools, although some PA days differ between elementary and secondary students. items.title: Another poll suggests mayoral race in Mississauga is between 3 candidates
items.summary: A second poll this week suggests the mayoral race in Mississauga has turned into a three-candidate contest as voters prepare to cast their ballots on Monday. Results from a new Liaison Strategies Mississauga Tracker survey released Thursday morning show former mayor Bonnie Crombie leading with 35 per cent among decided and leaning voters, followed by city councillor Alvin Tedjo at 31 per cent and the incumbent, Mayor Carolyn Parrish, at 28 per cent. City councillor Dipika Damerla received four per cent, while two per cent would choose someone else. Liaison Strategies, a national public opinion research firm, surveyed a random sample of 1,000 Mississauga residents from Oct. 19-20, using Interactive Voice Recording technology. Participants were reached through random digit dialing across landline and cellular networks. 1 percentage points, 19 times out of 20, and is higher for subsamples, including decided and leaning voters, the pollster said. items.title: Three businesses ordered to close after health inspections in Mississauga
items.summary: Three businesses have been ordered to close in recent weeks following health inspections in Mississauga. The results have been posted on the Peel Health Inspections website. Officials said Lhasa Ink Tattoos, located at 104-2465 Cawthra Road, just north of The Queensway, was ordered to shut down after an inspection on Oct. 6. Barbie Doll Lashes, located at 1830 Dundas Street East in the city’s east end, failed an inspection on Oct. 16. And Peel Public Health said Perfect Brows by Yaris, also located at 1830 Dundas Street East, was ordered to close after an Oct. 16 inspection. Officials said the businesses were not in compliance for several requirements: In each case, the business was ordered to close immediately. It’s not clear when they may reopen. items.title: Mississauga’s mayoral race a close three-way contest with Bonnie Crombie pulling ahead, a new poll shows
items.summary: The Mississauga mayoral race is one to watch on election night, with a narrow three-way race between the front-runners. From left, incumbent mayor Carolyn Parrish, current councillor Alvin Tedjo and former mayor Bonnie Crombie are in an epic battle for the top job in Mississauga. Heading into Monday’s municipal election, Mississauga’s mayoral race remains a close three-way race, with former mayor Bonnie Crombie pulling ahead of incumbent mayor Carolyn Parrish, according to a new poll from Liaison Strategies. Meanwhile, current councillor Alvin Tedjo has moved from third place to second, past Parrish, as his campaign lauds the momentum of the “teal wave” in reference to his election sign colour. When accounting for undecided voters, Crombie was at 27 per cent, Tedjo at 24 per cent and Parrish at 21 per cent with 24 per cent undecided. Among decided and leaning voters, Crombie was at 35 per cent, Tedjo at 31 per cent and Parrish at 28 per cent. items.title: Distraction thefts on the rise in Mississauga, Brampton and across Ontario
items.summary: They appear friendly, but their intentions are sinister. They might pretend to be lost and innocently in search of a kind and helpful person to provide directions. Or, they simply come off as an amiable sort striking up a brief conversation in a parking lot with a stranger. Whatever the specific ruse, the crooks police call distraction thieves most often operate in pairs, have ill intentions and move quickly in picking out and then stealing from their victims — many times approaching in a car, other times on foot. Peel Regional Police say distraction thefts have risen dramatically in Mississauga and Brampton the past couple of years — from 25 reported incidents in 2024 to 222 reported thefts in 2025. So far this year, 266 such thefts have been reported to police in Peel’s two major cities. The significant rise in distraction thefts has prompted police in Peel to dedicate more resources — and officers — to combatting the crime. Investigators say they’re also looking at possible links between incidents in Peel and similar thefts reported in other parts of Ontario. Distraction thefts, which mostly target older adults, are on the rise across the province, police in other municipalities report.

items.title: With Debates Behind Them, Four Mayoral Hopefuls Make Their Final Push Before Mississauga Votes
items.summary: Insauga.com reports Mississauga voters head to the polls on Monday to elect a mayor, 11 city councillors and a slate of school board trustees, after a campaign season that featured heated debates among the leading mayoral candidates. According to the outlet, the mayoral race's four main contenders, incumbent Carolyn Parrish, former mayor Bonnie Crombie, and city councillors Alvin Tedjo and Dipika Damerla, are competing within a larger field of 14 hopefuls for the city's top elected office. The outlet reports Parrish and Crombie traded pointed attacks during the campaign's debates, while some polls and campaign watchers suggest Tedjo has recently gained additional support. According to insauga.com, it remains to be seen whether that momentum is enough to turn the race into a close three-way contest on election night. The outlet reports record numbers of residents already cast ballots during advance polling earlier this month, and remaining voters can cast their ballots on Oct. 26 at any location within their own ward. According to the outlet, winning candidates will serve a term running from 2026 to 2030.

items.title: Most expensive home sets sales record in Mississauga
items.summary: A luxurious private estate that just changed hands has officially broken the record for the most expensive home sold not just in Mississauga, but across the entire Region of Peel. Today, Sam McDadi Real Estate Brokerage announced it broke its own record with the city and region’s highest residential sale in history. 1 million, which was set at the Saint George Mansion (2275 Doulton Drive). “It’s been off-market for several months and I had an internal buyer who was quite interested, and we ended up getting two offers,” Sam McDadi told INSAUGA Canada. “It set a record for pricing that’s similar to the Bridal Path, which is great for our city,” he added, referring to the ultra-affluent Toronto neighbourhood that’s famously home to Drake and other well-known Canadian artists and moguls. Following on the heels of the Saint George Mansion, the multi-million-dollar sale is, McDadi says, a sign that Mississauga is a city that luxury homebuilders and buyers should pay attention to. ’’ While McDadi’s team says the exact price and address aren’t being revealed at this time, McDadi can share that the property, massive in size and full of rare amenities, has a special feel. “The architectural design and layout are fantastic. When you walk in there, you realize you have a special property,” he says, adding that the house is relatively new and was custom-built with top-notch touches.
